$comment: The app's calls into its own Python half (hermes_android.call). Each call takes a JSON object with exactly its params and answers either its reply or {"error": <words for the user>}. Events are the lines the Python half emits on its own (hermes_android.event_line); secrets are the keystore variable names both halves use. Types: string, integer, boolean, string? (string or null), [T] (a list of T), or an enum or a record below. The Kotlin side is generated from this file (scripts/android/gen_bridge_contract.py). `blocking: true` marks a call that may wait on the network; the app runs it apart from the core's frames, so it is not ordered with them or with other calls.

runtime_facts.summary: The interpreter facts the app shows.

secrets_changed.summary: The keystore changed: re-read its secrets; variables it no longer holds are revoked.

gateway_start.summary: Starts the gateway in the :gateway process; state changes arrive as events.

gateway_stop.summary: Asks the gateway to drain and stop; 'stopped' arrives as an event.

gateway_state.summary: The gateway host's state in this process.

save_custom_endpoint.summary: Adds a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint to config.yaml (Dv20), or replaces the saved one id names (null for a new one); a new key goes to the keystore under key_env, an edit without one keeps the entry's key_env; forget names the endpoint's own keystore slot when config.yaml no longer names it after this save (the app forgets it, as for a delete), else null.

list_custom_endpoints.summary: The custom endpoints saved in config.yaml (providers.*), without keys: has_key says whether one is in the keystore under the entry's key_env.

delete_custom_endpoint.summary: Removes a saved custom endpoint from config.yaml; names the keystore variable the app deletes (always the endpoint's own HERMES_CUSTOM_<ID>_API_KEY, never another provider's), and whether the default model was detached from it.

probe_endpoint.summary: The server behind an address (URL, host:port or a bare host on the known ports) and its models; the key, if any, is used for this probe only.

discover_endpoints.summary: OpenAI-compatible servers on the phone's Wi-Fi network (its /24 at most, the known ports), each with its models.

ssh_new_key.summary: A fresh Ed25519 identity; the app stores private in the keystore at once.

ssh_public_key.summary: The public half of the identity the core reads from the keystore.

ssh_host_key.summary: A host's key, seen without logging in, and how it stands against known_hosts.

ssh_trust_host.summary: Pins a host key the user confirmed; refuses over a different pinned key.

ssh_configure.summary: Points the terminal at the host (config.yaml terminal.*, Dv32).

ssh_check_login.summary: Logs in once with the app's key against the pinned host key.

terminal_status.summary: Where the terminal runs: user@host:port on an SSH host, null on the phone.

terminal_local.summary: Runs the terminal on the phone again (config.yaml terminal.backend, Dv32); the host stays pinned.

telegram_configure.summary: Sets the one Telegram user the bot answers (config.yaml telegram.allow_from, Dv32).

telegram_status.summary: Whether a token is held, who may talk to the bot, and whether this build has the Telegram SDK.

telegram_check.summary: Asks Telegram who the held token belongs to: ok (bot named), refused by Telegram, or Telegram out of reach.

gateway_state.summary: One state change of the :gateway process's gateway host, as a JSON line through native.emit; reason only for failed.
